captions: Chapter seven. The quiet one.
The names so far command tens of thousands of
crores. Our next winner proves you can play this
game brilliantly with a fraction of that.
The name Dolly Khanna is famous in Indian markets
— though the portfolio is actually run by her
husband, Rajiv, and that's worth saying plainly.

Their disclosed book holds just about ten stocks,
worth
a little over two hundred crore rupees.

Tiny, by star-investor standards — and that's the
lesson.

They hunt unloved cyclical companies — chemicals,
metals, sugar,
textiles — and buy them before the market cares.
Prakash Industries. GHCL. SOM Distilleries.
Then they hold, quietly, for years, and sell into
strength when the crowd finally arrives.
Low turnover. High patience. No noise.
It's a reminder that the method scales down —
you don't need a fortune to invest like this.
You need temperament.
Let that sink in.

A ten-stock portfolio, run patiently, quietly, from
home —

outperformed the vast majority of loud, leveraged
'experts' online.
The edge was never the size of the account.
It was behaviour. And behaviour is the one thing
you can copy for free.
